title: Symphony Ltd - 517385 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Symphony Q1 FY27 consol revenue rose 8% to ₹378 crore; adjusted PAT up 23% to ₹43 crore, with management warning of near-term margin pressure from input costs.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 8% YoY to ₹378 crore and EBITDA reported was ₹48 crore (up 26%), but management said June 2026 included a ₹5 crore one-time non-cash charge while June 2025 had ₹9 crore of exceptional income; on that basis EBITDA was ₹53 crore vs ₹38 crore and PAT ₹43 crore vs ₹35 crore. Domestic India revenue grew 15% and modern trade grew over 100%, which management attributed largely to general trade channel inventory being cleared last year. Gross margin was 49.8% and EBITDA margin 12.6%, but management guided to short-term margin pressure from elevated commodity and plastic costs, with only partial price pass-through. Australia (CTPL) remains weak, with management committing to no further capital deployment.

financial_highlights.change: ex ₹5 crore non-cash charge in Jun-26 and ₹9 crore exceptional income in Jun-25
vs ₹37 crore reported; adjusted ₹24 crore in Jun-25
core capital employed ₹73 crore vs ₹136 crore
vs ₹363 crore; after ~₹225 crore repaid to Australia and loans

segments.name: Bonaire USA
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹36 crore vs ₹27 crore (up 35%); EBITDA ₹18 crore vs ₹7 crore; PAT ₹17 crore. Growth driven by scale-up of air cooler models, sold as rebranded Indian SKUs to Home Depot and Lowe's.

segments.name: IMPCO Mexico
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹54 crore vs ₹66 crore; EBITDA ₹3 crore vs ₹7 crore; PAT ₹1 crore. Management cited two consecutive mild summers (2025 and 2026).

segments.name: GSK China
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹34 crore vs ₹24 crore (up 43%); EBITDA ₹6 crore vs ₹2 crore; PAT ₹5 crore. Standalone entity now debt-free after repaying debt and interest to Symphony India.

segments.name: CTPL Australia
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹27 crore vs ₹31 crore; EBITDA negative ₹4 crore vs negative ₹2 crore. Reported PAT of ₹36 crore includes ~₹42 crore one-time gain from sale of Bonaire USA shareholding and IPRs, excluded at consol level.

segments.name: BISP (Beyond India Summer Products)
segments.commentary: Consol TTM sales about ₹560 crore (~48% of consol revenue); standalone TTM ₹179 crore (~23%), with EBITDA near double-digit margin. Mix includes large-space ventilated air coolers, tabletop fans, water heaters and exports.

segments.name: Symphony Brazil
segments.commentary: Not a season in the quarter; no material update given.

guidance_outlook: Management expects short-term margin pressure from elevated input costs (plastic, commodities); quantum not quantifiable yet and depends on how long the war lasts.
Price hikes of 7% to 10% taken outside household coolers; no hike yet in household cooler segment; further hikes planned but extent uncertain.
Management expects Mexico and USA sales to grow significantly in summer 2027 if summer is normal or robust; no numeric target given.
Bonaire USA and GSK China expected to perform well in the current quarter (Q2 FY27), then more muted; Bonaire USA little revenue in the following two quarters.
No inventory overhang at trade or company level as of June 30, 2026; primary off-season buying by channel partners expected in current and subsequent quarters.
capex_capacity: No further capital allocation to CTPL Australia; management said Australia turnaround to be done without deploying additional capital.
Interim dividend of ₹1 per share (face value ₹2) declared for the quarter, total payout about ₹7 crore.
Impairment and write-off at CTPL Australia recorded in FY26; management said it is behind the company.
GSK China and Bonaire USA sell through company-owned or retail warehouses in the US; no new capacity commissioning details given.
demand_pricing: India revenue grew 15% despite pre-summer channel inventory overhang; modern trade (including e-commerce, D2C, large formats) grew over 100%, and modern trade is over one-third of India revenue, with profitability close to general trade.
General trade carried elevated channel inventory from the prior year, which depressed company sales to them; management does not expect 100% modern trade growth to continue.
Standalone exports from India declined due to geopolitical and shipping disruptions; Middle East remains affected and buyer sentiment muted by higher landed costs.
Q1 demand was patchy in North and East India due to uneven weather; no secondary sales expected in the coming quarter, only primary off-season buying.
Coolers in the US are used outdoors and as whole-house or window-mounted units, sold through Home Depot and Lowe's; management said US and Mexico sales were helped by a hot Southwest summer.

qa_highlights.question: What share of sales comes from modern trade and e-commerce, and how does its profitability compare with general trade?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not disclose the exact share for competitive reasons. Modern trade (including e-commerce, D2C, large formats and regional stores) is over one-third of India top line, with general trade at 60-65%. Modern trade profitability is almost comparable to general trade.

qa_highlights.question: Will input cost inflation such as plastic hit margins in coming quarters, or will it all be passed on given low channel inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin pressure is expected in the short term because costs remain elevated and depend on how long the war lasts. Symphony will pass on some but not all of the increase; the impact is hard to quantify yet despite value engineering.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the modern trade growth above 100%: share gain, market growth, strategy change, or low base?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly the absence of channel inventory in modern trade and e-commerce, versus general trade which carried elevated inventory from the prior year. Management said growth of this scale is unlikely to continue.

qa_highlights.question: What SKUs are driving Bonaire USA growth, and how does its distribution differ from Australia?
qa_highlights.answer: Products are rebranded Indian SKUs, led by the Air Force model, sold to Home Depot and Lowe's, aided by a hot Southwest US summer. Bonaire uses a US warehouse and retailer model, whereas Australia sells mostly to installation companies, with retail still small.

qa_highlights.question: Could you give revenue, EBITDA and PAT for all subsidiaries?
qa_highlights.answer: Bonaire USA revenue Rs36 crore (vs Rs27 crore), EBITDA Rs18 crore (vs Rs7 crore), PAT Rs17 crore. IMPCO Mexico revenue Rs54 crore (vs Rs66 crore), EBITDA Rs3 crore (vs Rs7 crore), PAT Rs1 crore. GSK China revenue Rs34 crore (vs Rs24 crore), EBITDA Rs6 crore (vs Rs2 crore), PAT Rs5 crore. CTPL Australia revenue Rs27 crore (vs Rs31 crore), EBITDA negative Rs4 crore, reported PAT Rs36 crore including about Rs42 crore one-time gain that is excluded at consolidated level.

qa_highlights.question: What price hikes have been taken and what is planned, given raw material inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: No price hike yet in the household cooler segment. Outside household coolers, 7% to 10% hikes have been taken, with more planned in coming days; the extent depends on when the war ends and costs normalise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the strategy to turn around CTPL Australia?
qa_highlights.answer: No additional capital will be deployed; the impairment and write-off is treated as history from FY26. Management said there is nothing new on product, distribution or manufacturing beyond what is already in place.

qa_highlights.question: What are the BISP product categories beyond exports, and are tabletop fans and water heaters sold online or offline?
qa_highlights.answer: BISP includes large-space ventilated air coolers, tabletop fans (sold year-round), water heaters and exports. Management said these are already in modern retail and GT in top cities, but not yet nationwide. BISP is about 48% of consol revenue and 23% of standalone TTM revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why is there demand for air coolers in the US, a developed market with high per-capita income?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said coolers are not seen as a poor man's AC outside India and are sold in the US, Europe and the Middle East. In the US they are used outdoors, as whole-house or window-mounted units in the dry Southwest, and their key advantage is portability and plug-and-play use.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Mexico and USA sales, given the summer conditions?
qa_highlights.answer: Mexico had two consecutive mild summers (2025 and 2026), so management expects significant growth in summer 2027 if conditions are normal or robust, without giving a number. USA sales should also rise next summer if the summer is similarly good.

qa_highlights.question: Have export shipments resumed, and are geopolitical issues affecting orders?
qa_highlights.answer: The Middle East remains affected. Higher costs elsewhere have made buyers more cautious, since landed costs rose and they cannot pass on the full increase, so purchases are muted and not yet back to normal.

qa_highlights.question: What is the subsidiary outlook for the next few quarters, and what are secondary sales trends in July and early August?
qa_highlights.answer: Bonaire USA and GSK China should be fairly good in Q2 FY27 and more muted after that, with Bonaire seeing little revenue in the next two quarters. Q1 was patchy in North and East India. No secondary sales are expected in the coming quarter; only primary off-season buying by channel partners in the current and subsequent quarters.

risks_watch: Short-term gross and EBITDA margin pressure from elevated plastic and commodity costs, with only partial price pass-through; quantum not yet quantified and tied to how long the war lasts.
Price hikes outside household coolers (7% to 10%) are in place, but household cooler pricing is not yet taken; further hikes are uncertain.
Modern trade growth above 100% is driven by the absence of channel inventory and is not expected to repeat; general trade growth is needed to sustain volumes.
Middle East exports remain disrupted and buyer sentiment is muted by higher landed costs; the export recovery timeline is unclear.
CTPL Australia revenue continues to soften; the turnaround is to be achieved without additional capital, with no quantified target.

Weather dependence: Mexico and US sales depend on a robust summer 2027, and North and East India demand was patchy in Q1; Bonaire USA is expected to have little revenue in the two quarters after Q2 FY27.
key_quotes: As you can observe the gross margin despite all headwinds and geopolitical situation and pressure on commodity prices and also inventory overhang due to bad summer of '25, we have marginally increased the gross margin percentage to 49.8% , while EBITDA margin percentage to 12.6%.
So, in the short term, margins are likely to be impacted.
As of 30th June '26 i.e. our season -end, there is no inventory overhang either at a trade level or at a company level, it is completely normalized.
So, it's only in India that, we view coolers as a cheaper alternative to air conditioners.
The point is that we are very clear internally and also to assure all the shareholders that whatever impairment or write-off is the history that's not going to happen.
summary.management_tone: Confident on domestic momentum, the balance sheet and the BISP diversification, but cautious on near-term margins and exports. Management was reluctant to quantify the margin hit or price increases and deferred to the path of the war and input costs. It was also evasive on modern trade share, citing competitive reasons.

growth.why: No numeric revenue guidance; management warned of near-term margin pressure from input costs with partial price pass-through, expects Bonaire USA and GSK China to perform well in Q2 FY27 then soften, and has no capacity additions or expansion discussed; reported Q1 revenue +8% and reported EBITDA +26% (adjusted for one-offs, EBITDA roughly +39%).
